result.keywords: This article examines low-visibility delivery routing for autonomous harbor shuttles operating in fog-prone coastal districts. A hybrid scheduling model combines beacon-based localization, tide-aware path constraints, and stochastic parcel prioritization to reduce missed drop-offs during weather disruptions. Simulation results compare centralized dispatch with edge-assisted routing under variable lamp density and dock congestion, showing improved on-time delivery for time-sensitive medical and perishable shipments. The study also proposes a lightweight safety protocol for shared pedestrian corridors and evaluates its effect on energy use and route stability in evening operations.
result.title: Aurora Parceling in Coastal Fog Logistics Networks.
